text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Savings bank CEC raised to 105 percent interest rates on deposits.
- Roamnia's state radio posted deficit of 19 billion lei in 1996.
- Restructuring in Romania's industrial sector should start with the country's regies autonomes.
- The Transport Ministry will import 1,500 second-hand buses for urban transport.
- The Craiova-based Daewoo-Automobile Craiova will export first batch of 500 Cielo cars to Russia.
- The recent move of commercial banks to increase interest rates on deposits made the national currency more attractive, the paper says.
- IAIFO Zalau engineering company will sack 700 employees.
- The restructuring of the SNCFR railway authority will not affect number of staff, Transport Minister Traian Basescu is quoted as saying.
- The Transport Ministry plans to suspend transports of raw materials to Sidex SA steel plant in Galati, following the plant's failure to pay its debts to the ministry.
- Lower chamber of Deputies endorsed bill giving foreigners the right to buy land in Romania.
- Costs related to a possible Romanian integration into NATO could amount to some $35 million a year, the paper says.
- Copper mine at Rosia Poeni almost closed following power cuts oredered by the state-run Renel RA electricity utility.
- The Brasov-based Roman SA truck plant will be split in several production units following its restructuring, the paper says.
